extracted.intended_audience: administrators, public officials, legal practitioners, courts and persons affected by administrative action in South Africa
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for lawful, reasonable and procedurally fair administrative action under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act (PAJA) 2000 (South Africa), including notice-and-comment, public inquiries, reasons, judicial review grounds, remedies, time limits, regulations and training obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'administrative action'
rubrics_metrics.description: Any decision taken, or any failure to take a decision, by an organ of state when exercising constitutional or public powers/functions, or by a natural or juristic person when exercising a public power or performing a public function in terms of an empowering provision, which adversely affects the rights of any person and which has a direct, external legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes an inclusive list of acts (making orders, giving certificates, issuing licences, imposing conditions, retaining articles, etc.) and expressly lists exclusions (specified executive powers of National/Provincial Executive, municipal council executive powers, legislative functions, judicial functions, decisions to institute/continue prosecution, certain decisions under Promotion of Access to Information Act, etc.). 'Empowering provision' is a law, rule of common law, customary law, agreement or instrument in terms of which the action was purportedly taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirement of procedural fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative action which materially and adversely affects the rights or legitimate expectations of any person must be procedurally fair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a procedure is fair depends on the circumstances of each case. Part of a core obligation imposed on administrators; links to specific procedural steps required in section 3(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate notice of nature and purpose of proposed action
rubrics_metrics.description: A person affected must be given adequate notice of the nature and purpose of the proposed administrative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the specific procedural minima to give effect to the right to procedurally fair administrative action (section 3(2)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable opportunity to make representations
rubrics_metrics.description: A person affected must be given a reasonable opportunity to make representations about the proposed administrative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a specific procedural minimum (section 3(2)(ii)); may include written or oral representations depending on circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear statement of the administrative action
rubrics_metrics.description: A person affected must be given a clear statement of the administrative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps the person understand what decision is contemplated or taken and forms part of the minimum procedural requirements (section 3(2)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate notice of right of review or internal appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A person affected must be given adequate notice of any right of review or internal appeal, where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrators must inform affected persons of available review or appeal mechanisms (section 3(2)(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate notice of the right to request reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: A person affected must be given adequate notice of the right to request written reasons for the administrative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of minimum procedural information to be provided (section 3(2)(v)); links to section 5 on requesting reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional procedural opportunities (assistance, representation, dispute, appearance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrators may, in their discretion, allow affected persons to obtain assistance and, in serious or complex cases, legal representation; to present and dispute information and arguments; and to appear in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are discretionary measures an administrator may provide to give practical effect to procedural fairness (section 3(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted departure from procedural requirements where reasonable and justifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrator may depart from any of the section 3(2) requirements if it is reasonable and justifiable in the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deciding whether a departure is reasonable and justifiable, the administrator must account for factors including: objects of the empowering provision; nature and purpose of the administrative action; likely effect of the action; urgency; and the need to promote efficient administration and good governance (section 3(4)(a)-(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to follow other fair procedures where empowered
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an administrator is empowered by an empowering provision to follow a procedure that is fair but different from section 3(2), the administrator may follow that different procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognises statutory or other procedural schemes that achieve fairness without mirroring section 3(2) exactly (section 3(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator's duty when action affects the public (choice of procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an administrative action materially and adversely affects the rights of the public, the administrator must decide whether to hold a public inquiry, follow a notice-and-comment procedure, both, another prescribed fair procedure, or another appropriate procedure giving effect to section 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator must actively choose the most appropriate public-facing procedure to secure fairness (section 4(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inquiry procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a public inquiry is held the administrator must conduct it or appoint suitably qualified person(s); determine a procedure that includes a public hearing and complies with prescribed procedures; conduct the inquiry accordingly; compile a written report and give reasons for any action taken or recommended; and publish a concise summary of the report and inspection particulars in the Gazette (and communicate the information by other effective means).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets content and publication obligations to ensure transparency and public participation in inquiries (section 4(2)(a)-(b)(i)-(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-and-comment procedure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If notice-and-comment is chosen, the administrator must take appropriate steps to communicate the administrative action to those likely to be materially and adversely affected and call for comments; consider any comments received; decide whether to take the action with or without changes; and comply with prescribed notice-and-comment procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the essential steps for a notice-and-comment process (section 4(3)(a)-(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted departure from public-procedure requirements where reasonable and justifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrator may depart from the requirements for public inquiries or notice-and-comment if reasonable and justifiable, considering factors such as the objects of the empowering provision; nature and purpose of the action; likely effect; urgency; and need to promote efficient administration and good governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors the departure/factors framework in section 3(4) applied to public procedures (section 4(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to request written reasons (timing and duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person whose rights have been materially and adversely affected and who has not been given reasons may, within 90 days after becoming aware (or reasonably expected to have become aware) of the action, request written reasons; the administrator must, within 90 days after receiving the request, furnish adequate reasons in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets 90-day request and response periods (section 5(1)-(2)); the timings can be varied under section 9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption where administrator fails to furnish adequate reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: If an administrator fails to furnish adequate reasons, it shall, subject to subsection (4) and absent proof to the contrary, be presumed in judicial review proceedings that the administrative action was taken without good reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates evidential consequence in judicial review for failure to give adequate reasons (section 5(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted departure from duty to furnish reasons (and factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrator may depart from the requirement to furnish adequate reasons if reasonable and justifiable and must forthwith inform the requester; in determining reasonableness, factors include objects of the empowering provision, nature/purpose/likely effect, nature/extent of departure, relation between departure and its purpose, importance of the purpose, and need to promote efficient administration and good governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the test and required notification for departing from the reasons duty (section 5(4)(a)-(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic reasons regime by Ministerial notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister may, at an administrator's request, publish a list by Gazette specifying actions or classes of actions in respect of which the administrator will automatically furnish reasons to affected persons without a request; the Minister must publish such list within 14 days and at the administrator's cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits streamlining by pre-designating classes of actions where reasons are provided automatically (section 5(6)(a)-(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for judicial review — lack of authority, unauthorised delegation, bias
rubrics_metrics.description: A court or tribunal may review an administrative action if the administrator was not authorised by the empowering provision, acted under an unauthorised delegation, or was biased or reasonably suspected of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the core categories of reviewable defects; appears as section 6(2)(a)(i)-(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for judicial review — failure to comply with mandatory and material procedure/condition
rubrics_metrics.description: A court or tribunal may review if a mandatory and material procedure or condition prescribed by the empowering provision was not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance with critical statutory/processual prerequisites can invalidate action (section 6(2)(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for judicial review — procedural unfairness
rubrics_metrics.description: A court or tribunal may review if the administrative action was procedurally unfair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 6(2)(c) — links back to the section 3 procedural fairness requirements; procedural unfairness is an independent ground of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for judicial review — materially influenced by an error of law
rubrics_metrics.description: A court or tribunal may review if the administrative action was materially influenced by an error of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where legal mistake affects the substance of the decision (section 6(2)(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for judicial review — improper reasons and motives (including irrelevant/relevant considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A court or tribunal may review if the action was taken for a reason not authorised by the empowering provision, for an ulterior purpose or motive, because irrelevant considerations were taken into account or relevant considerations were not considered, because of the unauthorised dictates of another person or body, in bad faith, or arbitrarily or capriciously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated in section 6(2)(e)(i)-(vi); captures a range of improper motivational or consideration-based defects in decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for judicial review — action contravenes law or not authorised
rubrics_metrics.description: A court or tribunal may review if the action itself contravenes a law or is not authorised by the empowering provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as section 6(2)(f)(i) and overlaps with lack of authority/ulterior purpose grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for judicial review — irrationality / lack of rational connection
rubrics_metrics.description: A court or tribunal may review if the action is not rationally connected to the purpose for which it was taken, to the purpose of the empowering provision, to the information before the administrator, or to the reasons given by the administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 6(2)(f)(ii) with subpoints (aa)-(dd) — establishes rational connection/justification standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for judicial review — failure to take a decision and unreasonable delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person relies on failure to take a decision, review may be instituted where an administrator has a duty to take a decision and has failed to do so (either where no statutory period is prescribed but delay is unreasonable, or where a prescribed period has expired without the decision having been taken).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 6(3) provides specific routes for review of failure to decide, including claims of unreasonable delay and instances where a statutory period has expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for judicial review — so unreasonable no reasonable person could have acted
rubrics_metrics.description: A court or tribunal may review where the exercise of the power or performance of the function is so unreasonable that no reasonable person could have so exercised the power or performed the function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures the Wednesbury-type irrationality/unreasonableness standard (section 6(2)(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for judicial review — otherwise unconstitutional or unlawful
rubrics_metrics.description: A court or tribunal may review where the action is otherwise unconstitutional or unlawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all ground in section 6(2)(i) for other constitutional or legal defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and internal remedies for judicial review proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings for judicial review must be instituted without unreasonable delay and not later than 180 days after either the conclusion of internal remedies or the date the person was informed of/aware of the action and reasons; internal remedies in other law must generally be exhausted before review unless the court, in exceptional circumstances, exempts the person in the interests of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets limitation period (180 days) and exhaustion requirement, with an exceptions power for courts; Rules Board to make procedural rules (section 7(1)-(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies available in judicial review proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts or tribunals may grant any just and equitable order, including directing the administrator to give reasons or to act as required; prohibiting particular conduct; setting aside the action and remitting with or without directions; in exceptional cases substituting or varying the action or directing compensation; declaring parties' rights; granting temporary interdict or other temporary relief; and orders as to costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For failures to take decisions, courts can direct taking of decisions and make other appropriate orders (section 8(1)-(2)). Remedies are flexible and equitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variation of statutory time periods by agreement or court
rubrics_metrics.description: The 90-day periods in section 5 and the 90- or 180-day periods in sections 5 and 7 may be reduced or extended for a fixed period by agreement between the parties or, failing agreement, by a court or tribunal on application where interests of justice require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanisms for consensual or judicial adjustment of time limits (section 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and training of presiding officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Heads of administrative regions or magistrates at head of regional divisions must designate in writing magistrates as presiding officers for designated Magistrate's Courts; take reasonable steps to designate at least one presiding officer per designated magistrate's court; presiding officers must perform functions assigned under this Act; the South African Judicial Education Institute must develop and implement training courses for presiding officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes duties around designation and training to ensure competent presiding officers for PAJA proceedings (section 9A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations and code of good administrative conduct (Ministerial duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister must make regulations relating to procedures to be followed by designated administrators and in relation to classes of administrative action to promote procedural fairness, procedures for public inquiries, notice-and-comment procedures, and requests for reasons. The Minister may also make regulations about an advisory council, drafting protocols, education programmes, and other matters; and must publish a code of good administrative conduct to provide practical guidelines for administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations and the code must be submitted to/approved by Parliament (and in some cases Cabinet) before Gazette publication; regulations that may result in state financial expenditure require consultation with the Minister of Finance. The code must be approved before publication and is intended to provide practical guidance to promote efficient administration (section 10 and 10(5A)-(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory council functions (regulatory guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations may establish an advisory council to monitor application of the Act and advise the Minister on matters such as publishing uniform rules/standards, improvements to internal complaints/appeals and judicial review, appropriateness of tribunals, lapsing of rules and standards, public and administrator education programmes, and other improvements to ensure conformity with administrative justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists matters on which the advisory council may advise, including compilation of registers of rules/standards and recommending specialised tribunals (section 10(2)(a)(i)-(viii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial power to exempt or permit variation of application of sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister may, by notice in the Gazette and if reasonable and justifiable, exempt an administrative action or class of actions from application of any of the provisions of sections 3, 4 or 5; or permit an administrator to vary any of the requirements referred to in section 3(2), 4(1)(a)-(e),(2) and (3) or 5(2), in a manner specified in the notice; any exemption or permission must be approved by Parliament before Gazette publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorises targeted exemptions/variations for reasonableness and efficiency, but requires parliamentary approval (section 2(1)-(2) and section 4(4) cross-reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-faith liability protection
rubrics_metrics.description: No person is criminally or civilly liable for anything done in good faith in the exercise, performance or purported exercise/performance of any power or duty under the Act or rules made under section 7(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides limited legal protection for administrators acting in good faith under the Act (section 10A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short title and commencement formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act is titled the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act, 2000 and comes into operation on dates fixed by Presidential proclamation as published in the Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the formal naming and commencement mechanism (section 11 and commencement notes).
